A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MVCustom with the same authors, task, and core framework. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original customization experiments, quantitative comparisons in Tables 2–4, qualitative ablations, and latent-completion examples across seeds.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical results and adds computational-cost measurements, quantitative component ablations, shape-control experiments, and a depth-estimation failure analysis.

M1.justification: The core architecture, training procedure, rendering, completion, and Algorithm 1 are retained. Appendix D.1 adds an inference variant that uses pose-conditioned transformer blocks during early denoising steps and then switches to the original backbone blocks, providing a limited procedural extension for shape customization.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the WebVid10M training subset and CO3Dv2 customization coverage, including the stated 14-concept, 16-prompt evaluation. The added studies vary inference components within the existing task; car-shape customization already appears in v1 Figure 6. No distinct dataset, population, or task expansion is established.

E2.justification: The displayed comparisons retain SEVA-based Custom Img + Img-MV gen, CameraCtrl with DreamBooth-LoRA, and CustomDiffusion360, together with the existing CameraCtrl control experiment. However, v2 Appendix C.1 newly announces a CustomNet evaluation without identifiable corresponding results or a labeled comparison. Its actual addition to the evaluated baseline set cannot be verified.

E3.justification: Reference-image fidelity changes from comparison against all reference images in v1 Appendix D.2 to a randomly sampled subset matching the generated-image count per prompt in v2 Appendix C.2. v2 also adds time, memory, and COLMAP reconstructed-point measurements and explicit pose-conditioning schedules for the new ablations. The revised description does not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v1 provides qualitative component ablations in Figure 5. v2 substantially extends this evidence with quantitative inference-component ablations in Table A3, additional examples in Figure A2, pose-conditioning schedule sensitivity in Appendix D.1/Figure A3, and a depth-quality failure comparison in Figure 6.

E5.justification: Both versions already report plus/minus values and the same six-seed completion-diversity examples, moved from Figure 7 to Figure A4. v2 rounds Table 2 uncertainty values and adds similarly formatted ablation results, but introduces no new repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Existing comparison values are retained apart from rounding, but substantial new results are reported. Table 2 adds inference costs, including 130.92 seconds and 19.29 GB for MVCustom. New Table A3 reports pose accuracy of 0.543, 0.768, and 0.771 for customization alone, added rendering, and added completion, respectively, alongside other metrics. New qualitative results expose shape-control and depth-estimation failures.

T1.justification: The task formulation, rendering equations, mesh construction mathematics, and camera-pose accuracy definition are unchanged. v2 numbers the existing accuracy equations as Equations 5–8 but adds no theorem, proof, formal assumption, or substantive mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract replaces the exclusive claim that MVCustom is the only framework achieving both capabilities with a claim of balanced, consistently competitive performance. The task and method contributions remain unchanged, and the introduction and conclusion retain the stronger exclusivity claim, making this a localized qualification.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands interpretation and limitations: it explains computational overhead, dependence on depth-estimation quality, pose-conditioning tradeoffs, and trajectory-density/CFG effects. It also interprets completion's reduced perceptual similarity alongside improved geometric measurements. The existing canonical-pose limitation is retained and expanded with a reported unsuccessful cross-attention intervention.

D1.justification: v2 specifies 50 reference images for the DreamBooth-LoRA baseline, explicitly confirms eight-frame quantitative evaluation, and recommends CFG around 5 while identifying flickering around 7.5. These improve implementation guidance without establishing changes to previously reported training. The main hardware, training budgets, pseudocode, and project link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Eight references are added, chiefly concerning camera-controlled diffusion transformers and depth estimation. Appendix A.1 expands the comparison with DiT-based approaches, while Section 5 connects depth-related failures to other methods. The main related-work section and overall novelty positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: Most introductory and methodological prose is unchanged. Local rewrites expand architectural justification and evaluation explanations; limitations move into Section 5, the CameraCtrl control receives its own subsection, and appendices are reorganized. Conference headers, affiliation formatting, acknowledgements, and broader-impact wording also change.

P2.justification: The visual evidence expands substantially through new Figures 6, A2, and A3 and Table A3, while Table 2 gains a computational-cost column group. Figure 1's annotations and layout are updated. Existing style and diversity figures and supplementary comparison tables are retained under new appendix numbering rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the paper by quantifying previously qualitative component ablations, exposing computational costs, and illustrating depth and shape-control limitations. These additions improve empirical support and practical transparency. The gain is limited by unchanged main benchmark evidence, a reference-sampling revision unreconciled with unchanged reported scores, and the unsupported announcement of a CustomNet evaluation. The abstract is more measured, although stronger exclusivity claims remain elsewhere.
